source.title: Augmented Large Language Models with Parametric Knowledge Guiding
source.authors: Ziyang Luo; Can Xu; Pu Zhao; Xiu-Bo Geng; Chongyang Tao; Jing Ma; Qingwei Lin; Daxin Jiang

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports downstream-task scores across language-model and knowledge-guider sizes, which bear on V6, but does not measure pretraining loss or reproduce a loss-scaling law.
record.gate_note: The paper's main experiments evaluate knowledge-guided prompting, not scaling laws. Rows record the model-size comparisons in Table 7 and the knowledge-guider size comparisons in Table 3. Other task scores, which do not vary model size, are omitted. No held-out pretraining cross-entropy, training-token or compute sweep, power-law fit, extrapolation test, or compute-optimal allocation is reported.
record.test_reason: A knowledge-guiding method paper, not a scaling study. Its Table 7 and Figure 3 sweep of four InstructGPT API models (0.3B to 175B) gives downstream scores with and without guidance. That bears weakly on V6: no loss, no fit, no prediction. Table 3 varies the size of the guider module inside the pipeline, which measures the authors' own system component rather than a model's downstream performance, so it does not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that larger target LMs benefit more from PKG and that small LMs fail even with relevant knowledge, which they tie to emergent abilities, calling LLM scale 'a critical factor'. They also say larger PKG modules perform better, 'consistent with the scaling law' of Kaplan et al.; this is a citation, not a test.
record.recipe_differences: Downstream-task accuracy and exact-match comparisons across selected model sizes, rather than held-out pretraining-loss measurements and power-law fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported target-model size trends vary by task and by whether PKG guidance is used; some intermediate scores are flat or non-monotonic. OPT PKG scores rise across the tested sizes on all four reported tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The PKG+davinci system score rises with guider-module size (OPT 0.3B to 2.7B) on all four tasks, and LLaMa-7B scores higher still.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a generate-then-read pipeline, larger knowledge-generator modules yield better downstream system accuracy.

record.problems: The size sweeps report selected sizes and downstream benchmark scores only; they provide no uncertainty estimates or fitted prediction curves. Model families differ in the PKG comparison that includes LLaMa-7B.
record.rows_left_out: No additional size-sweep result rows omitted; non-size-varying task comparisons were left out because they do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No loss power law in other regimes.
No relation of downstream scores to pretraining loss, no fitted or predicted curve, and no uncertainty estimates. Sizes are only four API models of unconfirmed size and training.
No exponents or fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: InstructGPT sizes (0.3B, 1.3B, 6.7B, 175B) are the authors' attributions, and the four API models may differ in training beyond size, so size is confounded. There is no uncertainty reporting and only four points per series. The paper has 'tests' status only marginally; a reviewer could reasonably classify it as T4 or cites_only.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
No pretraining-loss/downstream-performance relationship or fitted predictive scaling curve is tested; only downstream scores across selected model sizes are reported.
No fitted exponents, fitting choices, or bends in loss curves are examined.

relationships.condition: InstructGPT sizes with PKG guidance on FM2, and 175B vs smaller on all tasks
relationships.reason: FM2 with PKG rises monotonically (38.0, 45.4, 52.0, 67.3), and 175B scores highest on every task (T7-PKG-*-FM2, T7-*-Davinci-*).
relationships.display_finding: FM2 scores with PKG increased monotonically through 38.0, 45.4, 52.0, and 67.3, while 175B scored highest on every task.

relationships.condition: InstructGPT 0.3B to 6.7B on NQ-Table, MedMC-QA and ScienceQA, and direct FM2 at 1.3B
relationships.reason: Scores are flat at about 0 or near chance, or drop with size, before a jump at 175B. The authors frame this as emergence, not smooth predictable gains (T7-D-Babbage-FM2, T7-*-NQ, T7-*-Med, T7-*-Curie-Sci).
relationships.display_finding: Scores remained near zero or chance, or declined across smaller models, before a jump at 175B that the authors described as emergence.
